<!-- The "Architect robustness into the workflow" slide body. Lives out here
     for the same reason the figures do: it is a two-column build with five
     beats on each side, and inline it buried the surrounding slides. The
     heading and the `.notes` stay in index.qmd; this file is everything
     between them.

     ONE example, five readings. Every card on the right is the SAME EV Sales
     document used in the efficiency act and on the diff slide below, so by the
     time the room gets here they already know these lines. Do not swap in a
     second example: the argument is that one artifact survives all five checks.

     Each beat shows ONLY the part that step touches — the failing render, the
     failing check, the rows that changed, the computed lines. Beats 4 and 5 are
     the SAME artifact twice: 4 shows the hand-typed numbers being replaced by
     the calls that compute them, 5 drops the diff and shows the result, with
     those two lines washed yellow because a computed value is CONTENT. Red/
     green is a claim about an EDIT; yellow is a claim about the VALUE, so the
     colour change is the argument moving from "you can see it" to "it comes
     from the data." Keep the two cards' lines and variable names identical. An earlier
     version kept the whole source block pinned above every beat; it was five
     lines of already-read text sitting on top of the one line that was new, and
     the eye had to hunt for the change.

     `.robustness` has exactly TWO direct children, `.stack` and `.demo`. It is
     a 2-column grid, so every extra direct child gets auto-placed into the next
     free cell — an earlier version put the individual beats in here as siblings
     and they laid out as stack1|stack2, stack3|stack4, ...

     Left: ONE stack, not one copy per beat. Each step is `fragment custom`,
     which reveal leaves visible at rest (`.fragment:not(.custom)` is what hides
     a fragment), so the whole workflow is readable from beat 0 and a click only
     moves reveal's `.current-fragment` class down the list.

     Right: the claim first, then the card that backs it. The claim is the
     sentence John says out loud, so it reads before the artifact rather than
     as a caption after it. Every card lives in ONE grid cell (`.panels > *` is
     `grid-area: 1/1`), so nothing moves as the beats swap, and the claims do
     the same above it. Both regions reserve a floor in slide px, because
     `current-visible` hides with `visibility` — the box stays in flow, but an
     empty region would otherwise collapse.

     Card chrome is the deck's own `pre.specimen` (see custom.css): `.diffcard`
     for source, `.errcard` for tool output, `.sp-del`/`.sp-add`/`.w` for the
     changed rows, `.steps-up` for the yellow computed-value highlight. Nothing
     here invents a second visual idiom for what the deck already draws.

     NEVER write a live inline-R span on this slide -- not in a card, not in
     this comment. knitr runs before pandoc and evaluates backtick-r anywhere in
     the file, HTML comments included, so it would try to resolve ev_sales and
     fail with "object 'ev_sales' not found". Both backticks are escaped as
     &#96;. -->

::: {.robustness}

<!-- Fenced divs, not raw <div>s, because the icons are shortcodes: Quarto
     expands the fa and quarto shortcodes in markdown, and a raw HTML block
     passes straight through unexpanded. Each mark names the TOOL that step is
     about, which is the only reason they earn their space here — four of the
     five are marks the room already reads instantly, and the robot stands in
     for the one thing with no canonical logo. They inherit `currentColor` from
     `.step`, so they dim and light with it.

     NEVER write a shortcode's braces in a comment on this slide, not even as
     an example. Quarto expands shortcodes inside HTML comments -- the same trap
     as backtick-r below -- so an argument-less `fa` written here reaches
     fontawesome.lua with no icon name and kills the render with
     "Cannot get Attr from TypeNil". Name the shortcode in words instead. -->
::: {.stack}
